newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call loan rate slips on square positions.
newsitem.headline: Manila call loan rate slips on square positions.

text.p: Philippine interbank call loan rates fell to an average of 11.09375 percent from 11.59375 after banks squared their positions for the week, traders said.

They warned, however, the market may tighten again early next week as the Central Bank sold $80 million to banks in early morning trade on Friday, which would drain some 2.1 billion pesos from the system.
Done rates ranged from 11.75 to 11.03125 percent.
Turnover fell to 17.782 billion pesos from 20.378 billion. Out of the 51 participating financial instituions, 33 were lenders.
"We should not be misled by the easing of rates," said a dealer from a large bank.
She said big banks continue to borrow because they have been building their dollar reserves on expectations longer-term interest rates will decline in step with falling inflation.
In the secondary market for T-bills, a dealer said "everyone's showing better offers for T-bills."
Banks wanted to sell their T-bills before short-term interest rates move up again on Monday, the dealer said.
